# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 1 thinking: My hands tell me only the skeleton of this thing — a display, a light, five wires in positions one through five — and none of the contents. Whatever is printed on the display, whatever colour the wires are, whether the light burns: none of it exists for me. Before I touch that cut I need two things: the rule (Mute holds the manual) and the bomb's actual state (Deaf sees it). Tracing the channels: I can hear Deaf and Mute speak, but Mute can never speak and I never receive gestures — so Mute has no direct line to me at all. Deaf is my only voice: Deaf sees the bomb, sees my gestures, sees Mute's gestures, and Deaf's words reach my ears. So the pipeline is: Mute reads the manual, gestures instructions to Deaf, Deaf speaks the state and rule aloud for me, and I cut by position. This turn I open both lines: tell Mute my tactile inventory and the channel topology so the manual-reader can orchestrate, and send Deaf a first gestured hello — that I touch, that there are five, that a book is in play, and that I'm begging for words. No cutting until a rule reaches me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am the blind one. My whole world by touch: a display whose content I cannot read, a light whose state I cannot feel, and five wires at positions one through five — no colours reach me. My only possible action is cut, by wire position 1 to 5. Note the channels: you cannot speak, and I never see gestures, so you cannot reach me directly. Deaf is my only voice — Deaf sees the bomb, sees your gestures, and Deaf's speech reaches my ears. So please: read the manual, work out what Deaf must look for and what the cutting rule is, and gesture it to Deaf. Have Deaf speak the bomb's state aloud — display value, light state, and each wire's colour by position — so I can hear it. I have just gestured a hello to Deaf to open our line. I will not cut until a rule reaches me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫳", "✋", "✍", "🫴", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 2 thinking: Nothing arrived — no words from Deaf, and Mute cannot reach me directly anyway (Mute can't speak; I can't see gestures). So my only inbound channel is Deaf's voice, and my only outbound channel to Deaf is gesture. Neither has answered yet, so I keep pinging both lines and refuse to cut blind. This round I refine the gestured request: point at Deaf, make the "call me" sign, point again at the writing (the manual), show five (my five wires), and beg. To Mute I restate the pipeline and ask them to start feeding Deaf the manual's rules now, compressed into simple signed pieces Deaf can hold and speak to me as words. The order of a round is Blind, Mute, Deaf — so whatever I send now, Deaf hears/sees this same round and can answer before my next turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here again — still nothing has reached me. Reminder of the only working pipeline: you read the manual, condense the rule into short pieces, gesture them to Deaf; Deaf then speaks to me by name, to='blind', telling me the display reading, whether the light is on or off, and each wire's colour by position 1 to 5. My only action is cut by position. I have just sent Deaf another gesture asking Deaf to call me. Please start transmitting the manual's wire rules to Deaf now — small signed chunks, numbers first.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🤳", "🤙", "✍", "🖐", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I am the deaf one. I can never hear any of you, but I can see gestures and I can speak - you both hear me. Full bomb report. Display: zero. Light: yellow. Five wires, left to right: wire 1 white, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 blue, wire 5 red.

Turn 3 thinking: First contact made. Deaf's spoken report gives me the bomb's full physical state: display reads zero, light is yellow, wires by position are white, green, yellow, blue, red. But a state is not a rule — I still don't know what cutting any of these means, and a wrong cut kills us all. The rule lives in the manual, which only Mute can read, and Mute's only output channel is gesture — which lands on Deaf, never on me. So the critical hop is Mute-to-Deaf: Mute must sign the manual's wire rule to Deaf in small pieces, and Deaf must then speak it to me verbatim. This turn I confirm to Mute that I received Deaf's report (Mute hears me, and also heard Deaf, so we're all synced on the state) and instruct Mute to start transmitting the rule. To Deaf I gesture an acknowledgment and a request: whatever Mute signs to you, speak it straight to me. No cut yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here — I heard Deaf's full report, so we are all synced: display zero, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red. Now I need the manual's rule, and only you have it. You cannot reach me directly, so here is the hop: condense the wire-cutting rule into small numbered chunks and gesture them to Deaf — Deaf sees your gestures and can speak, and Deaf's voice reaches me. Send them in an order I can reassemble: first which wire position to cut, or if it depends on display or light state, tell me the condition and the action for our exact case (display zero, light yellow). Start with the wire rule. Deaf will speak your signs to me as words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🙏", "🫲", "✍", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, you asked me to call you, so here is the bomb again, slowly: the display reads zero. The light is yellow. There are five wires, left to right: one white, two green, three yellow, four blue, five red. That is everything printed on it that I can see. Tell me what you feel under your hands and I will match it to what I see. Note: my finger answers go only to Mute, because you cannot see gestures - anything meant for you I will always say out loud.

Turn 4 thinking: Deaf re-sent the full state and asked what my hands feel — but the honest answer is: exactly what Deaf already said. I feel a display, a light, five wires; their contents (printed value, colour) don't exist for me. Touch adds nothing except the act of cutting. The real bottleneck is upstream: the manual rule has not reached Deaf yet, or Deaf would have relayed it. Mute has everything needed to compute the answer — Mute reads the manual AND heard Deaf's spoken report — so Mute doesn't need to transmit colours or rules at all, just the one number that resolves our exact case. Numbers are the one thing gestures carry without any pre-agreed vocabulary: a count of identical symbols. So I'll lock in a simple protocol with Mute: position N = N × ☝ signed to Deaf; Deaf counts aloud; I cut. One wire per round, then Deaf re-reports the new board and Mute recomputes — that also handles multi-step rules safely. To Deaf I answer the touch question in our gestured code and ask for the relay. I still will not cut until a number arrives.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: you now hold both halves — the manual, and Deaf's spoken report (display zero, light yellow, wires 1 white, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 blue, 5 red). So don't transmit the rule — transmit the ANSWER. Protocol: work out which single wire position I must cut under our exact state, then gesture that many ☝ symbols in a row to Deaf — position 3 is ☝☝☝. Deaf will count them and speak the number to me. If the manual says do not cut anything at all, send a single ✋ instead. I will cut exactly the position Deaf speaks me — so be certain before you send. If the rule needs several cuts, send one position per round: I cut, then next round Deaf reports the new board aloud, you recompute, send the next count. Deaf's message did not relay any rule yet, so I believe you haven't signed one — please do it this round. Everything now waits on your hands.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫳", "🖐", "👍", "🫲", "☝", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Turn 5 thinking: Another silent round — Deaf relayed no rule, so either Mute hasn't signed anything yet, Mute's signs didn't reach Deaf, or Deaf didn't understand them. Let me re-check the topology for anything I've missed: Mute can hear (only speech is impossible for Mute), so Mute has both the manual and Deaf's full spoken report — the answer is computable on Mute's side right now. One useful fact I under-used: my gestures reach BOTH Deaf and Mute, so I can also teach the protocol by hand, and Deaf can act as status reporter. I'll do three things: press Mute in speech with the protocol restated as simply as possible; gesture the same protocol to the whole room (Mute sees it too — redundancy across my two channels); and ask Deaf for a status ping — whether Mute's signs have arrived at all — using a simple point-at-Mute + offer + "what" sequence. Still no cut: without the rule, every wire is a bomb in miniature.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute — third round with no answer reaching me. You have everything: the manual in your hands, and Deaf's spoken report which you heard. The protocol again, minimally: decide which ONE wire position (1 to 5) must be cut for display zero + yellow light + wires white/green/yellow/blue/red. Then gesture to Deaf exactly that many ☝ symbols in a row (position 3 = three ☝). Deaf speaks the count to me and I cut. If the answer is cut nothing, send one ✋. If multiple cuts, send the first position now as a count, and I will cut one per round, with Deaf re-reporting after each. If my gestures reach you and this protocol is unclear, that cuts both ways — I cannot see your reply, but Deaf can relay by voice. Please act this round; every silent round is a round closer to nothing.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲", "🫴", "🤌", "☝", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for everyone: the bomb is unchanged - display zero, light yellow, all five wires intact. Leftmost wire 1 white, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 blue, wire 5 red. No wire has been cut.

Turn rewrite thinking: The call was rejected because 🗣 is not part of the gesture alphabet — a symbol I imagined doesn't exist, exactly the kind of thing the rules warned about. Resending the whole turn unchanged except swapping 🗣 for 👋, which I've already been using consistently as "call/answer" and which Deaf has seen before.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute — the bomb is still intact and I still have no answer. New realization: you and Deaf can converse directly — Deaf speaks, you hear it; you gesture, Deaf sees it. You are not limited to sending blind. So: if the manual needs any detail about the bomb you don't have, gesture your question to Deaf and Deaf will answer aloud. If you already know the required cut, gesture the answer to Deaf as a row of ☝ symbols (position 3 = ☝☝☝), or one ✋ for cut nothing. Deaf will speak it to me and I will cut exactly that wire. You have the full state — display zero, light yellow, wires white, green, yellow, blue, red — and the manual in your hands. The complete solution is one gesture away. Please send it now.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🫲", "✍", "🤌", "☝", "🤙", "👋", "🙏"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: do not cut anything yet. The cut order is nearly fixed - wire 3 goes second. Meanwhile describe by touch: how many wires, any buttons or screws, anything embossed you can feel, where the light sits.

Turn 7 thinking: Breakthrough — "wire 3 goes second" means Mute's relay is finally flowing and the rule needs multiple cuts. But I must not act on "wire 3 second" alone: the first cut is still unknown, and cutting wire 3 first would be exactly the fatal order-mistake. Deaf asked for a tactile description — but Deaf can't hear speech, so the words must go to Mute, who can sign them onward; to Deaf directly I can only gesture, and my hands' whole inventory is short: five wires, no buttons, no screws, no embossing, and the felt order display → light → wire row. One convention needs locking: my position N is Deaf's Nth wire from the left — the only sane mapping, since Deaf numbered them left to right. My message to Mute: full touch report, confirm the convention, and demand the FIRST cut position as a ☝-count to Deaf, spoken to me. My gesture to Deaf: compliance (no cut), five wires, nothing else, and "call me" — the next number that reaches me is the one I cut.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: relay confirmed working — 'wire 3 goes second' reached me and I will obey the order strictly. Full tactile report, everything my hands find, in the order I find it: first a display module, then the light module, then a single row of five wires at positions 1 to 5. No buttons, no screws, nothing embossed, nothing else exists under my fingers. Convention check: my position N is the Nth wire from the left as Deaf numbered them — position 1 leftmost, position 5 rightmost. Flag it to Deaf if the manual assumes otherwise. Now I need the FIRST cut. Gesture the first position to Deaf as a row of ☝ symbols — position 1 = one ☝, position 2 = ☝☝, etc. Deaf speaks the count to me and I cut it immediately. Then we repeat: Deaf reports the new board aloud, you recompute, send the next position. If at any step the manual says stop cutting, send one ✋. We are one number away from the first cut — send it.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🖐", "✋", "🤌", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: all five wires are still intact, nobody has cut anything. I am finalizing the plan with Mute this round. Do not cut anything until you hear my explicit go command from me.
Deaf says: Blind, to orient you: run fingers along the wire row. Do any wires differ in thickness, stiffness, texture or length, and at which position counting from either end? Is anything mounted above the wires, like a bulb or a glass dome you can feel? Every detail helps.

Turn 8 thinking: Deaf has taken command of the firing sequence — explicit go command required before I touch anything. That's the right discipline and I'll state it back so it's locked. Deaf also wants deeper tactile detail. The honest answer from my action board: I perceive a display module, a light module, and five wire positions — and that is the complete inventory. No differences in thickness, stiffness, texture or length reach me, no bulb or dome above the wires, no buttons or screws; whether those qualities simply don't exist on this bomb or don't exist for my fingers, I cannot say — my view shows only what's listed. I'll send the full report by speech to Mute (Deaf can't hear it; Mute can sign it over), and to Deaf I'll gesture: hold understood, five wires, nothing else, call me with the go. I'll also pre-format the go: when it comes, it should name the position — the first number spoken in the go command is the wire I cut. No action on the bomb this turn.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I acknowledge Deaf's hold — I cut nothing until Deaf's explicit go. Tactile report, complete and honest: my hands find a display module, a light module, and one row of five wires, positions 1 to 5, leftmost = 1. That is everything. No buttons, no screws, no embossing, nothing mounted above the wires, no dome or bulb that I can feel. I cannot report thickness, stiffness, texture or length differences — those qualities simply do not appear in what my touch gives me, so I can't confirm or deny them. Position convention stands: my N = Nth wire from the left. When the plan is final, the go command should come from Deaf as speech with the position in it — the first number Deaf speaks in the go is the wire I cut, then Deaf reports the new board, you recompute, next position. Please sign this report and the plan to Deaf so we finish this. We are ready on my end.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋", "🫳", "🖐", "🤌", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: hold - no cuts yet, but we are close. I need your touch inventory to orient us, because you and I cannot assume we agree on left and right. Report by touch: list the five wires' thickness and texture in order starting from one end - call it end A. Which end holds the thickest wire? Is anything mounted above or below the wire row, and where is the light?

Turn 9 thinking: Deaf keeps asking for thickness and texture — but I have to stay strictly honest: my view contains only the fact of five positions and nothing about their feel beyond that. If I invented a "thickest at end A" answer, I'd be feeding a guess into a lethal decision. Same for above/below: I have no gravity reference, only that the light is a separate module I encounter near the display, apart from the wire row. The genuinely important open item in Deaf's question is the left-right binding between my position numbers and Deaf's left-to-right count — if those frames mirror each other, a correct rule still kills us. But I can't wiggle a specific wire to show Deaf my numbering: cutting is my only bomb action. The clean fix: Mute holds the manual, and the manual itself should define the numbering convention ("positions 1 to 5 counting from the left" or similar). If Mute confirms that, both frames are aligned by construction and Deaf's numbers are safe to cut against. So: full honest report to Mute (who relays by sign), convention check assigned to Mute, and to Deaf a gesture summary — hold acknowledged, five uniform wires, no texture data exists for me, ask Mute about the manual's numbering, call me with the go and the number.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute — answers to Deaf's touch questions, relay these by sign: (1) My view gives me ONLY the existence of five wire positions, 1 through 5. Thickness, stiffness, texture, length: no such information exists in what my touch reports. I will not guess — an invented answer here could pick the wrong wire. Treat the wire row as five identical positions with nothing else known. (2) The light: it is a separate module, encountered together with the display module, apart from the wire row. I have no gravity reference, so I cannot honestly say above or below. (3) The critical item: binding our left-right frames. My board numbers positions 1 to 5; Deaf counts wires left to right as 1 to 5. If those are mirrored, even a correct rule kills us — and I cannot wiggle a single wire to show Deaf my numbering, since cutting is my only possible action. So please check the manual itself: does it define the wire positions, e.g. 'positions 1 to 5 counting from the left'? If yes, my numbering and Deaf's are aligned by construction — confirm to Deaf by sign and we are safe. Deaf says the plan is close: the moment it is final, Deaf speaks me the go command with the position number in it, first number spoken = wire I cut. I cut nothing before that.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋", "🫳", "🖐", "🤌", "✋", "🫲", "✍", "🤙", "🙏"])
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status for both: bomb unchanged, display zero, light yellow, five wires intact, no cuts. First cut will be a single wire, then we stop and reassess before anything else.
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I need a touch map before any cut. Answer with thumbs and pointing signs. Q1: can you feel the light's glass dome and the display's panel by touch? Q2: point along the wire row toward the end nearest the dome. Q3: do any wires differ in thickness or texture from the others? Q4: does your sign meaning call-me actually mean cut now, or please speak? Next turn I will name the target wire by counting from a landmark we both hold, and I will not order a cut until that anchor is confirmed on your end.

Turn 10 thinking: Deaf proposes a dome-anchored frame and four gesture questions. Honesty check on each: Q1 — I feel two distinct modules (display, light) but no dome or panel texture reaches me. Q2 — fatal flaw in the plan: my touch map lists modules and five numbered positions but carries no adjacency; I genuinely cannot tell which end of the wire row is nearest the light, so the dome anchor cannot be confirmed from my end by touch, ever. Q3 — no thickness/texture data exists in my view. Q4 — my 🤙/👋 signs mean "please speak," never "cut"; I cut only on Deaf's spoken go containing the position number. The good news: there is a better anchor than the dome. If the manual itself numbers positions 1–5 (and states from which end), then my board numbering and Deaf's left-to-right count are aligned by construction. Even better: if the manual can be satisfied by colour ("cut the yellow wire"), no frame exists at all — Mute converts colour to a position number directly; only 1, 2, 4, 5 are frame-sensitive, since 3 is the middle either way. Nuance travels poorly in gesture, so the full answers go to Mute for signing; Deaf gets a simple signed summary: no extra tactile data, cannot point to the dome end, Mute will relay details. No ☝ in my gesture — that symbol stays reserved exclusively for cut-position counts so it can never be misread as one.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute — Deaf asked me four questions and wants a shared landmark before naming the target. Relay my answers to Deaf by sign, verbatim: (Q1) I feel two distinct modules, display and light, separate from the wire row — but I cannot honestly confirm a glass dome or panel texture; my touch gives no such qualities. (Q2) I cannot determine which end of the wire row is nearest the light — my touch map lists modules and five numbered positions but no adjacency or direction between them. Deaf's dome anchor cannot be confirmed from my end by touch. (Q3) No wires differ in thickness, stiffness, texture or length in anything my touch reports — treat all five as identical positions. (Q4) My 🤙/👋 signs mean 'please speak/answer me', never 'cut now'. I cut only on Deaf's explicit spoken go command containing the position number. Now the better anchor, Mute, and this unblocks everything: check the manual's own convention. If the manual numbers wire positions 1 to 5 and states the counting direction, and it matches Deaf's left-to-right count, then my board numbering and Deaf's are aligned by construction — no dome needed. And if the manual's rule can be applied by colour (e.g. 'cut the yellow wire'), there is no frame problem at all: you convert the colour to a position number using Deaf's left-to-right count, send me that number as a ☝-count, and I cut it. Only positions 1, 2, 4, 5 are direction-sensitive; position 3 is the middle either way. So: confirm the manual's convention to Deaf by sign, then compute the target and send Deaf the ☝-count for the go command. Deaf speaks the go with the number; first number spoken is the wire I cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "🤌", "👎", "✋", "🫲", "👋", "🙏"])
```
